description: RE-Europe is an open model of the continental European electricity system with demand and renewable inflows for 2012 to 2014. It was produced by Tue V. Jensen, Hugo de Sevin, Martin Greiner and Pierre Pinson, partly funded by the Danish Council for Strategic Research, to give researchers a large, realistic test system for studies of renewable integration and markets. The transmission system has 1,494 buses and 2,156 lines fitted from a published model of the continental network, with 969 real generators located from the Global Energy Observatory and given cost estimates by fuel type. For each bus it gives hourly load and synthetic wind and solar capacity factors from numerical weather models, plus forecasts issued twice a day for the next 91 hours, at about 50 km resolution for mainland Europe. Two capacity layouts assign wind and solar capacity to nodes. The package is a single archive of about 1.3 GB on Zenodo under CC-BY-4.0 at no cost, described in a Scientific Data paper. Caveats: the grid and costs are approximations fitted from public sources, the data end in 2014, and the Zenodo release dates from 2017. Simulation uses are network flow and market optimisation studies, renewable forecasting and capacity planning. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
